verses.2: Listen, you wise men, and pay attention, you who have knowledge.
verses.3: For the ear tests words, and the mouth tastes its food.
verses.4: Let us take judgment for ourselves, and know what is good among us.
verses.5: For Job said, "I am in the right, and God has taken away my justice."
verses.6: He has denied his own judgment; his arrow was shot without guilt.
verses.7: Who is like Job, who drinks mocking like water?
verses.8: Who has become a companion of evildoers and walks among the wicked?
verses.9: For he said, "God will not bring a person into judgment, nor will the Almighty consider the matter."
verses.10: Therefore, you of understanding hearts, listen to me. It is unthinkable for God to act unjustly, and the Almighty would not twist justice.
verses.11: For He gives to a man according to what he has done; and he finds the path of each man.
verses.12: Indeed, it is not true that God does what is wrong, or that the Almighty perverts judgment.
verses.13: Who has assigned dominion over the earth, and who has placed the whole world in order?
verses.14: If He sets His mind to it, He takes away His breath and His spirit returns to Him.
verses.15: Then all flesh together will perish, and man will return to the dust from which he was made.
verses.16: And if understanding listens to this, give ear to the voice of my words.
verses.17: Can a hater of justice be appointed ruler? Can a powerful man be declared guilty?
verses.18: Can one say to a king, "You are worthless"? Can a wicked man be called noble among nobles?
verses.19: For He does not show favor to rulers, nor does He recognize the voice of the mighty over the lowly, for all are His work.
verses.20: In a moment they die, in the middle of the night they are shattered, and the bold man is carried away without hand.
verses.21: For His eyes are on man's ways, and He sees all his steps.
verses.22: No darkness or shadow of death is a place of concealment for those who do evil.
verses.23: For He will not allow a man to go on in judgment to God.
verses.24: He breaks down the mighty, who had no knowledge, and raises up others in their place.
verses.25: Therefore He knows the work of the wicked, and will bring the night to pass, and they will be broken.
verses.26: He removes the wicked from their place, where they were seen.
verses.27: Because they turned away from Him and did not understand any of His ways.
verses.28: To bring upon them the cry of the poor and the cry of the needy He will hear.
verses.29: And He will remain silent, and who will accuse? Who will hide His face? And who will confront Him, whether concerning a nation or a man alone?
verses.30: For a corrupt king is worse than a tyrannical people.
verses.31: For it was said to God, "I have taken my oath, I will not be guilty."
verses.32: But apart from me, you will see me. If I have sinned, I will not add to it.
verses.33: May it be that He pays it back to you, for you have rejected it. You choose, and not I. What do you know? Speak.
verses.34: Let wise men among you speak to me, and a wise man listening to me will say:
verses.35: Job does not speak with understanding, and his words are not in wisdom.
verses.36: My father, test Job until the end, for his answers are among the wicked.
verses.37: For he adds to his sin, and between us his guilt is complete, and his words multiply toward God.

notes:
Notes
- v. 10: "It is unthinkable for God to act unjustly" reflects the Hebrew phrase *ḥālil lā 'el mi-rasha'*, which is best rendered as "It is unthinkable for God to act unjustly" rather than the more archaic "God is not a man that He should act unjustly."
- v. 17: The Hebrew *ḥāḇōš* is translated as "be appointed ruler" based on context, though it can mean "cover" or "conceal." The meaning here aligns with the idea of assigning authority.
- v. 32: The phrase *bəlĕaḏek yəḥezeh* is translated as "apart from me, you will see me" to preserve the rhetorical emphasis on self-awareness and accountability.
raw:
[1] Then Elihu answered and said:

[2] Listen, you wise men, and pay attention, you who have knowledge.

[3] For the ear tests words, and the mouth tastes its food.

[4] Let us take judgment for ourselves, and know what is good among us.

[5] For Job said, "I am in the right, and God has taken away my justice."

[6] He has denied his own judgment; his arrow was shot without guilt.

[7] Who is like Job, who drinks mocking like water?

[8] Who has become a companion of evildoers and walks among the wicked?

[9] For he said, "God will not bring a person into judgment, nor will the Almighty consider the matter."

[10] Therefore, you of understanding hearts, listen to me. It is unthinkable for God to act unjustly, and the Almighty would not twist justice.

[11] For He gives to a man according to what he has done; and he finds the path of each man.

[12] Indeed, it is not true that God does what is wrong, or that the Almighty perverts judgment.

[13] Who has assigned dominion over the earth, and who has placed the whole world in order?

[14] If He sets His mind to it, He takes away His breath and His spirit returns to Him.

[15] Then all flesh together will perish, and man will return to the dust from which he was made.

[16] And if understanding listens to this, give ear to the voice of my words.

[17] Can a hater of justice be appointed ruler? Can a powerful man be declared guilty?

[18] Can one say to a king, "You are worthless"? Can a wicked man be called noble among nobles?

[19] For He does not show favor to rulers, nor does He recognize the voice of the mighty over the lowly, for all are His work.

[20] In a moment they die, in the middle of the night they are shattered, and the bold man is carried away without hand.

[21] For His eyes are on man's ways, and He sees all his steps.

[22] No darkness or shadow of death is a place of concealment for those who do evil.

[23] For He will not allow a man to go on in judgment to God.

[24] He breaks down the mighty, who had no knowledge, and raises up others in their place.

[25] Therefore He knows the work of the wicked, and will bring the night to pass, and they will be broken.

[26] He removes the wicked from their place, where they were seen.

[27] Because they turned away from Him and did not understand any of His ways.

[28] To bring upon them the cry of the poor and the cry of the needy He will hear.

[29] And He will remain silent, and who will accuse? Who will hide His face? And who will confront Him, whether concerning a nation or a man alone?

[30] For a corrupt king is worse than a tyrannical people.

[31] For it was said to God, "I have taken my oath, I will not be guilty."

[32] But apart from me, you will see me. If I have sinned, I will not add to it.

[33] May it be that He pays it back to you, for you have rejected it. You choose, and not I. What do you know? Speak.

[34] Let wise men among you speak to me, and a wise man listening to me will say:

[35] Job does not speak with understanding, and his words are not in wisdom.

[36] My father, test Job until the end, for his answers are among the wicked.

[37] For he adds to his sin, and between us his guilt is complete, and his words multiply toward God. 

---

Notes
- v. 10: "It is unthinkable for God to act unjustly" reflects the Hebrew phrase *ḥālil lā 'el mi-rasha'*, which is best rendered as "It is unthinkable for God to act unjustly" rather than the more archaic "God is not a man that He should act unjustly."
- v. 17: The Hebrew *ḥāḇōš* is translated as "be appointed ruler" based on context, though it can mean "cover" or "conceal." The meaning here aligns with the idea of assigning authority.
- v. 32: The phrase *bəlĕaḏek yəḥezeh* is translated as "apart from me, you will see me" to preserve the rhetorical emphasis on self-awareness and accountability.
